    What is Tyson Fury diagnosed with?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Tyson Fury was diagnosed with bipolar disorder in 2017. The heavyweight boxer has openly discussed his struggles with mental health, including severe depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and previous substance abuse (alcohol and cocaine). His condition often manifests as extreme highs and low, sometimes referred to as "paradise syndrome". 
    In this video, Tyson Fury shares his experience with mental health and his journey towards recovery:
    1m
    ALL THE SMOKE FIGHT
    YouTube• Nov 2, 2018
    Key Aspects of Tyson Fury's Diagnosis & Struggles: 
    • Bipolar Disorder & Depression:
      Following his 2015 world title win, Fury entered a severe, multi-year depression, which he later identified as being part of bipolar disorder.
    • Mental Health Struggles: He has spoken openly about suicidal thoughts, anxiety, and the extreme, "low", and "high" moods associated with his condition.
    • Impact on Life & Career: His mental health battles led to significant periods of inactivity, retirement, and issues with alcohol and drug use.
    • Family Impact & Support: His wife, Paris Fury, has been vocal about the challenges of living with someone experiencing these intense mood swings, but noted the diagnosis brought relief by helping them understand his actions.
    • Management: While not "cured," Fury has focused on managing his mental health through professional help, support from his family, and returning to boxing. 
    If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please seek professional help or contact a helpline.
